docs.title: Documentation
docs.intro: Short and to the point — a cheat sheet, not a full manual.

overview.body:
Ranger is a lightweight self-hosted CI/CD hub for one personal server and a handful of trusted users: builds, a live log and step status in one place, no switching between tools.

The whole flow: add a project by SSH URL → set three commands (install/test/build) → trigger a build manually or on a schedule → watch the log live.

quickstart.intro: A full end-to-end test run — takes about 5 minutes and any git host (GitHub, GitLab, self-hosted).

steps.title: Create a test repository
steps.body: Set up an empty repo, e.g. ranger-hello-world, on GitHub or GitLab.

steps.title: Add one file and push it
steps.body: Locally: echo "console.log('Hello from Ranger')" > build.js, then git add, commit and push to that repo.

steps.title: Generate a dedicated SSH key
steps.body: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f deploy_key -N "" — a key just for Ranger, not your personal one.

steps.title: Add the key to the repository
steps.body: In the repo's settings, add deploy_key.pub as a read-only Deploy key.

steps.title: Create the project in Ranger
steps.body: "+ Add project" → paste the SSH URL and the deploy_key private key content → "Check repository" to pull the branch list.

steps.title: Fill in the Build command
steps.body: Set Build to node build.js, leave Install and Test empty — they'll be marked "skipped", not failed.

steps.title: Trigger a build
steps.body: "Create" → "Builds" tab → "Build". The live log should show "Hello from Ranger" with every step marked successful.

build.body:
One queue per project: builds of the same project never run in parallel, different projects run at the same time. Ranger clones the repo over SSH and runs install → test → build inside an unprivileged container with CPU/memory/process limits and a hard per-step timeout.

If a step fails, later ones are marked "skipped" and the build fails overall. The log streams to the UI over WebSocket and is saved to disk.

If both ports are filled in on the project ("Deploy" in the project form), a fourth step is added after a successful build: Ranger builds an image from the Dockerfile at the repo root, stops the project's previous container, starts the new one, waits for the port to open, and rolls back to the previous image if anything goes wrong. Without a Dockerfile in the repo, the deploy step fails with a clear reason in the log, without touching the container that's already running.

The second deploy mode is Docker Compose: an administrator enables it in project settings, and after the build Ranger runs docker compose up with a file from the repository and waits for every service to start. This mode has no rollback — on failure the services stay as they are, and the reason is in the build log.

users.intro: There's no registration: the first administrator is created at startup and adds everyone else.

steps.title: Set the administrator's email
steps.body: Put ADMIN_EMAIL in .env before the first start. It's only used on an empty database.

steps.title: Take the password from the log
steps.body: After startup run docker compose logs backend — the generated password is printed there once. Lost it? docker compose exec backend node dist/cli/reset-password.js <email>.

steps.title: Change it when you log in
steps.body: With an issued password the only thing you can do is change it: enter the issued one as the current password and set your own.

steps.title: Add everyone else
steps.body: People icon in the header → "Users": email and role (admin, operator or viewer). The password is shown once — pass it on personally.

security.body:
The private key is encrypted before it's stored and never comes back through the API in full — not in responses, not in build logs, even on a git error. The Docker socket is only reachable by the backend process and is never mounted into the build container.

The terminal is admin-only, requires re-entering your password right before a session starts (separately from your regular login), and every session opened is written to the audit log. A shell into a project's workdir runs in a throwaway container with no network access, dropped capabilities and the same CPU/memory/process limits as a build step — never on the host directly.

roadmap.body:
Deploy with automatic rollback (including a manual rollback to any earlier successful deployment), a list of host containers, scheduled builds and builds from a chosen branch, a read-only file browser for the latest checkout, host/container metrics, three roles (admin/operator/viewer) with user management, an audit log, an admin-only terminal and a public status page at /status are implemented.

The project moves in iterations: the first one (project → build → log), the second (deploy & containers) and the third (metrics) are done. The fourth (roles, audit, terminal) and the fifth (branches, status page, users) are implemented but haven't been checked on the server yet, so they aren't closed.

auth.noAccount: No account? Ask an administrator to create one.

account.title: Account
account.forceHint: {{email}} is using a password issued by the system. Change it to continue — enter the issued password as the current one.

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: There's no self-registration — accounts are created here. The generated password is shown once; the user must change it on first login.
users.rolesHint: admin — everything, including users, terminal and deploy keys; operator — builds, deploys, rollbacks, projects; viewer — read-only.
users.issuedHint: It won't be shown again. Pass it on personally — the user will have to change it on first login.

new.title: New project
new.name: Name
new.branchHint: Fill in the URL and deploy key above, then click "Check repository" to pick a real branch instead of typing it blind.
new.deployKeyHint: Generate a dedicated key: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f deploy_key. Add the public half to the repo as a read-only deploy key, paste the private half here — it's encrypted before it's stored.
new.commandsHint: Run in order inside an isolated container: install → test → build. Leave a field empty to skip that step. At least one command is required.
new.needCommand: Fill in at least one command — install, test or build
new.deployHint: Fill in both ports if the repository has a Dockerfile — after a successful build Ranger will build an image from it, stop the project's previous container and start a new one. Without a Dockerfile at the repo root, the deploy step fails with a clear error.
new.deployPortsRequired: Fill in both ports — container and host — or collapse the deploy section

edit.title: Edit project
edit.deployKeyHint: The key can't be edited partially — only replaced with a new one entirely.
edit.replaceDeployKeyWarning: The old key will be fully removed and stop working as soon as you save.
edit.revealDeployKeyHint: Only visible to admins. Recorded in the audit log every time.
edit.isPublic: Show on the public status page
edit.isPublicHint: Anyone without logging in will see the project name, status and time of its latest build — no logs, repository or branches. Page:
edit.deleteHint: Deletes the project entirely: settings, build and deployment history, the deploy key. If the project is deployed, its container is stopped and removed too. This can't be undone.
edit.deleteConfirm: Delete project "{{name}}" for good? This can't be undone.

env.title: Environment variables
env.hint: Passed to the install/test/build steps and to the deployed container. Values are stored encrypted and never shown after saving; long values are masked in the build log. Changes apply from the next build or deploy.
env.importHint: KEY=value format, one variable per line. Variables with an existing name get the new value.
env.revealHint: Visible to admins only. Every reveal is recorded in the audit log.

deployMode.title: Deploy mode
deployMode.containerHint: An image from the Dockerfile at the repository root; ports are set in project settings. Automatic and manual rollback.
deployMode.composeHint: After the build, docker compose up runs with a file from the repository: multiple services, their own volumes and networks. No rollback.
deployMode.composeFile: Path to the compose file in the repository
deployMode.composeWarning: A compose file can request privileged mode, the Docker socket, or mount any host path. Enable this only for repositories you trust as much as the server. Only an administrator will be able to change this project’s repository and branch.
deployMode.switchHint: Switching modes stops whatever was deployed in the old mode. The new mode takes effect from the next build of the main branch.
deployMode.changedByAdmin: An administrator changes the deploy mode.
deployMode.sourceLocked: This project deploys with docker compose — only an administrator can change its repository and branch.
